Projects / Implemented

Rydex — Vehicle Rental & Ride Booking Platform

Built a comprehensive vehicle rental and ride-booking platform supporting vehicle discovery, bookings, partner onboarding, payments with commission calculations, identity verification, real-time tracking, and communication.

April 2026

Problem & Solution

Problem

Vehicle rental and ride-booking marketplaces require complex orchestration: users need to discover nearby vehicles, partners need onboarding and verification, bookings need payment and commission handling, rides need real-time tracking, and all parties need secure communication.

Solution

Built a full-stack Next.js marketplace with geospatial vehicle discovery using GeoJSON, eight-step partner onboarding with video KYC, automated commission calculations, real-time ride tracking, OTP-based confirmations, and AI-powered messaging.

Key Engineering Features

Geospatial Vehicle Discovery

MongoDB 2dsphere index enables efficient proximity queries. GeoJSON stores vehicle locations; Leaflet displays results on interactive map. 10km radius search using $near operator.

Eight-Step Partner Onboarding

Progressive workflow guides partners through registration. Each step validates before advancing. ZegoCloud video KYC provides real-time identity verification with admin.

Platform Commission Engine

10% platform commission calculated on each booking. Earnings split: user payment → platform commission → partner earnings. Real-time calculation and transparent display.

OTP-Based Confirmations

Two-stage verification: pickup OTP confirms ride start; drop OTP confirms completion. Prevents fraud and creates audit trail.

Real-Time Ride Tracking

Socket.IO rooms per ride. Partner app broadcasts location updates; user sees live position on map. Optimized update frequency balances accuracy and performance.

Video KYC Integration

ZegoCloud enables real-time video calls between partner and admin for identity verification. Records verification status and timestamp.

Engineering Decisions & Tradeoffs

GeoJSON and MongoDB 2dsphere index for vehicle discovery

Rationale: Native geospatial support in MongoDB. 2dsphere index enables efficient proximity queries. GeoJSON is standard for geographic data.

Tradeoffs: MongoDB geospatial features are powerful but limited compared to PostGIS. For current scale, MongoDB is sufficient.

Multi-step onboarding workflow with state machine

Rationale: Complex onboarding requires progressive disclosure and validation. State machine ensures proper sequence and prevents skipping steps.

Tradeoffs: More complex than single form, but significantly better UX and data quality.

Platform commission calculated at booking time

Rationale: Commission rate might change; calculating and storing at booking prevents historical data issues. Clear separation of user payment, commission, and partner earnings.

Tradeoffs: Stored calculations use more space but provide accuracy and audit trail.

ZegoCloud for video KYC

Rationale: Specialized service handles video infrastructure complexity. Reliable video quality and recording capabilities.

Tradeoffs: Third-party dependency and cost; considered building custom but KYC reliability is critical.

Six Mongoose models for data separation

Rationale: Clear separation: User, Partner, Vehicle, Booking, Payment, Review. Easier to query and maintain than single combined model.

Tradeoffs: More models require more joins; used Mongoose populate for relationships.

OTP at both pickup and drop

Rationale: Two-party verification at critical transitions prevents 'ghost rides' and disputed completions.

Tradeoffs: Slight UX friction; considered GPS-based completion but OTP is more reliable.

Challenges & Solutions

Accurate geospatial search across varying locations

Solution: Implemented GeoJSON with proper coordinate order (longitude, latitude). Used 2dsphere index. Tested with various radius values to balance coverage and relevance.

Managing complex booking state across multiple actors

Solution: State machine with clear transitions: requested → accepted → pickup_confirmed → in_progress → drop_confirmed → completed. Each transition requires specific actor and event.

Commission calculations and earnings transparency

Solution: Store commission rate, user payment, commission amount, and partner earning at booking time. Display breakdown clearly in partner dashboard.

Eight-step onboarding without user fatigue

Solution: Save progress at each step; allow partial completion; clear progress indicator; estimated time remaining; skip non-critical steps initially.

Lessons Learned

  • Geospatial features require careful index configuration and understanding of coordinate systems
  • Multi-step workflows need clear state management and progress indication
  • Marketplace platforms require careful balance of user, partner, and platform interests
  • Commission and earnings calculations should be transparent and auditable
  • Video KYC adds trust but requires reliable infrastructure
  • Two-party verification (OTP) significantly reduces disputes and fraud
  • Real-time features create better UX but add complexity to testing and debugging
